lessonRef.focus: volume arguments for spheres and other solids
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: volume arguments for spheres and other solids

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Compare an oblique cylinder and a right cylinder with the same base area and the same height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8 and centre O. A point P lies 17 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 9.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 15.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 8; the tangent length is 15.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 15.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±3, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 8. Write its equation.
Compare a sphere of radius r and a cylinder of radius r and height 2r with two cones removed. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7 and centre O. A point P lies 25 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 18.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 24.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 7; the tangent length is 24.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 24.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±12, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 26. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±13, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.
